title: Christmas in Colmar 2026: market dates and a walk through the old town
description: Plan Christmas in Colmar in 2026 with confirmed market dates, three distinctive squares, a family friendly route and practical advice for an Alsace stay.
intro: Christmas in Colmar works best when you think of the old town as a collection of small markets connected by streets, rather than a single attraction with an entrance. The official Christmas website describes six markets, each with its own setting. You can sample three contrasting areas without making the day a race: the church square at Place des Dominicains, the waterfront around Petite Venise and the trading heart around Place de l’Ancienne Douane. Their different backdrops make revisiting a place after dark more rewarding than simply collecting more stops.

For 2026, the official practical information announces the main markets from 23 November to 29 December. That gives Colmar a useful advantage for a trip after Christmas, but it does not mean every concert, shuttle or attraction follows the same calendar. This guide builds a manageable walking day around the published market period. Treat side events as additions once their individual dates are confirmed, and keep an indoor meal or café break in the middle of your plans.

quickFacts.label: Suggested stay
quickFacts.value: One full day, preferably with an overnight stay

quickFacts.label: Route
quickFacts.value: Dominicains, Ancienne Douane and Petite Venise

sections.heading: Place des Dominicains: start with crafts and the church backdrop
paragraphs: Place des Dominicains gives a strong first impression of Colmar at Christmas because the wooden stalls sit beside the Dominican church. The official market guide highlights the building’s medieval stained glass and the effect of its lighting after dark. Begin with a circuit that looks at the square as a whole, then return to the stalls that interest you. Decorations are easier to compare when you have seen several makers, and you avoid buying the first fragile souvenir before spending the rest of the day protecting it.

A daytime visit helps you notice materials, colours and the architecture above the stalls. An evening return is about the illuminated setting, so the two visits need not repeat each other. If you want photographs, step aside from the main pedestrian stream and use the church as a landmark rather than trying to stop an entire queue. Families can agree on a meeting point at the edge of the square before browsing separately. The market description does not establish church visiting hours; check those independently if you want to go inside.

sections.heading: Petite Venise: a slower Christmas stop beside the Lauch
paragraphs: Petite Venise combines the half timbered houses along the River Lauch with a market that the tourism office presents as particularly suitable for children. The market area includes Place des Six Montagnes Noires; the riverside scenery extends beyond the stalls themselves. This distinction matters when following a map: a photo location beside the water and the activity you want may be a short walk apart. Allow time to enjoy both instead of expecting every familiar view to appear from one spot.

Make this the relaxed section of the route. Choose one snack or activity, then leave room for looking at the houses and water. The official description mentions children’s attractions, but their individual operation and any payments should be checked on arrival. Do not promise a child a specific ride or performance solely on the strength of a general market description. Near narrow passages and bridges, take turns making pictures and keep pushchairs moving where possible. A morning or early afternoon look is also useful if the evening crowds would make the waterfront uncomfortable for your group.

sections.heading: Place de l’Ancienne Douane: follow the old trading square
paragraphs: At Place de l’Ancienne Douane, the official guide places the stalls around the Schwendi fountain and towards the Koïfhus, the old customs building. This is a useful place to understand why the markets feel integrated into Colmar rather than installed in an unrelated open field. Look beyond the merchandise to the square’s changing angles, the building and the connections across the Lauch. Choose the fountain as an orientation point, but meet slightly away from it if the centre is busy.

The Koïfhus also appears in the official programme as an indoor craft market, separate from the outdoor square. If it is open during your visit, it can add a more focused look at local craft and a break from standing outside. Check the door information rather than assuming all indoor spaces follow the outdoor hours. This is a sensible place for a considered purchase after comparing earlier stalls. Ask how an item is made, whether it can be packed securely and how it will travel home before committing to delicate glass or ceramics.

sections.heading: Dates, meals and transport choices for a comfortable visit
paragraphs: The 23 November–29 December 2026 dates apply to the principal Colmar markets in the practical information reviewed for this guide. Christmas Eve has special hours: the official listing gives 11:00 to 17:00 on 24 December. Do not extend that closing time to other dates or assume nearby village markets share Colmar’s schedule. If your trip is built around one particular concert, boat performance or village excursion, check its own listing before booking accommodation around it.

An overnight stay makes the route easier because you can see the same squares in daylight and after dark without a rushed journey home. Compare the total cost of a central room with the cost and convenience of travelling in from elsewhere. For a rail visit, save the walk between your accommodation, the station and the old town before setting out. If driving, use the official parking and park and ride pages for current arrangements; seasonal restrictions and operating days can change, so an old screenshot is not enough.

Build your food budget around one proper seated meal and a smaller allowance for market tastings. Standing outdoors with several purchases is less comfortable than photographs suggest, particularly with children. Ask about ingredients and alcohol rather than relying on a product name, and check the return arrangements if a drink comes in a reusable cup. Wear shoes that remain comfortable on uneven paving, carry a compact waterproof layer and leave bulky luggage at your accommodation. Shorter loops are easier to adjust when weather or fatigue changes the plan.

itinerary: Morning: arrive with enough time to orient yourself before shopping. Begin at Place des Dominicains, inspect the craft stalls and note anything you might buy later. Continue towards Place de l’Ancienne Douane, using the Schwendi fountain and Koïfhus to understand the layout. If an indoor craft visit fits its opening hours, do it now rather than relying on a late return. This first circuit is for daylight detail and finding your bearings, not for trying every food stall.

Afternoon and evening: sit down for lunch, then continue to Petite Venise at a pace suited to the least energetic person in your group. Allow children a defined choice rather than promising every attraction. As daylight fades, return to the square whose architecture you most enjoyed, perhaps Dominicains for the church setting or Ancienne Douane for the illuminated Koïfhus. Finish with time to retrieve bags and reach your onward transport. For a second day, choose one separately checked village visit instead of adding several uncertain shuttle connections.

faq.question: Can I visit Colmar’s markets after Christmas in 2026?
faq.answer: Yes. The main market dates published by the official tourism site run to 29 December 2026. That does not confirm every associated activity through the same date. Check the specific event listing and restaurant availability if the days immediately after Christmas are the focus of your trip.

faq.question: Is one day enough for Christmas in Colmar?
faq.answer: One full day can cover the three areas in this route with a meal break. An overnight stay makes daylight and evening visits easier and gives you a second chance if rain changes your plans. A half day is better spent enjoying two areas carefully than rushing all six markets.

faq.question: Does the guide guarantee snow or performances on the canals?
faq.answer: No. Winter weather is variable, and a market season does not establish the dates of individual performances. Plan for the architecture, stalls and atmosphere that suit your visit, and only add a scheduled activity after checking its current listing. Bring clothing that also works in rain.

faq.question: Should I combine Colmar with several Alsace villages in one day?
faq.answer: Only if you are comfortable giving Colmar much less time. Each village has its own market days and transport arrangements. For a relaxed first visit, keep the main day in Colmar and choose one village for another day after checking the exact market and return connection.

conclusion: A good Christmas visit to Colmar depends on leaving space between attractions. Use the confirmed 2026 season to choose your dates, explore the three settings while there is daylight and return to one favourite square for its evening atmosphere. A realistic meal break and a reliable journey home will improve the experience more than squeezing another market into an already crowded day.
